#### Positive market sentiment sends prices higher 



- Major policy announcements by the European Central Bank, China’s central government and the Fed led to more positive market sentiment. Investors have been buying across all commodity markets and copper’s tight physical market fundamentals have come back into focus. 



- On September 7<sup>th</sup> , copper’s trading range was broken to the upside and, since then, the price has moved between $8,050/t and $8,445/t.  The arbitrage between COMEX and the LME accelerated in mid-September, but may now be levelling off. 



- Commercial spot business has not picked up after the summer holidays and the physical copper market remains extremely quiet in the US, Europe and in China.  Higher prices have led to an increase in scrap supply, which is also weighing on the cathode market.

Forecas|t productio|n allows| © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** October 2012 Copper Monitor www.crugroup.com #### Direction found In last month’s _Copper Monitor_ , we noted that the market was waiting for something to happen which would change the status quo and provide a direction for the price. This “something” came in the form of several notable policymaking decisions by the European Central Bank (ECB), China’s central government and the US Federal Reserve (the Fed). Taken together, these announcements boosted market sentiment, which has been sustained, at least at the time of writing. On September 7th , ECB President, Mario Draghi, announced that the bank would instigate a program of purchasing Eurozone members’ bonds in order to avert another sovereign debt crisis. On the same day, China’s National Development and Reform Commission announced that the central government would provide $157B in funding for 60 infrastructure projects that had not yet been launched due to a lack of local government financing. The copper market reacted positively to both of these announcements and the LME 3-month price rose high enough to break the upper bound of the trading range between $7,220/t and $7,820/t which had been in place since mid-May. While the ECB and Chinese announcements boosted confidence and moved the price, what solidified the market’s change in sentiment was the Fed’s announcement on September 13th that it would launch another round of quantitative easing (QE3). The catalyst for this action was the US employment report released on September 7th which showed little progress in terms of lower unemployment. QE3 took the form of a commitment by the Fed to buy an additional $40B of mortgage-backed securities every month, indefinitely. While this capital stimulus will certainly help to stabilize the mortgage market, the real shift in Fed policy was its statement that a “highly accommodative stance of monetary policy will remain appropriate for a considerable time after the economic recovery strengthens”. Essentially, the Fed has publicly committed itself to supporting US economic growth, which is a departure from the past. #### Investors buying once again Euro strength boosts LME copper

These policy announcements, by themselves, do not necessarily ensure that economic growth will accelerate and that metal demand will expand. However, from the standpoint of commodity market investors, who have been absent since May, these policies change the perception around both the future value of the euro (and, by association, the US dollar) and the rate of global economic growth. In terms of the euro, the ECB’s decision to create a sovereign debt bailout fund could not have occurred without the approval of EU governments. To an investor, this indicates that the Eurozone, in the future, may be less likely to experience the sort of banking and sovereign © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 19 October 2012 Copper Monitor www. crugroup.com debt crises that have occurred because institutional arrangements to avoid these are now in place. Thus, the euro is likely to be stronger, meaning that the US dollar will be weaker and commodity prices will tend to rise. The change in perception around global economic growth was made possible by the public shift in policy in both China and the US towards promoting and supporting economic growth. The selling finally stopped in mid-August, ahead of the central bankers meeting in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, and in anticipation of additional Fed action. Following the launch of QE3 on 13th September, investors began buying the commodity indexes, once again. Fund holdings of copper (red line) followed a similar pattern, but did not fall to the same extent as total index fund holdings. This is due to continued changes in the index weightings assigned to copper. Since weekly data on copper holdings are not published weekly by the CFTC, CRU estimates these holdings using both the CFTC report and information reported by the index funds themselves. However, the CFTC do publish end-of-month index fund holdings of copper and these reports confirm the weekly data estimates. The CFTC end-of-month reports show that fund holdings of copper decreased in March, April, May and June. They rebounded strongly in July, and were steady during August. The weekly CFTC Commitment of Traders report provides evidence that the

sentiment among copper speculators (managed money traders) is now more positive than negative. CFTC data for 4th September showed that managed money traders were essentially neutral (i.e. there were about as many shorts as longs). By 11th September, long positions outnumbered short positions. During the following two weeks, the net long held by these traders increased and, on 28th September, confidence that prices would rise, as indicated by the total long positions held, was at its highest level since 15th February 2011. The increased speculative inflows into the COMEX may help to explain why, since mid-September, the arbitrage between the COMEX and the LME prices in the nearby months has widened considerably. #### Spot market conditions relatively unchanged Despite more positive market sentiment and higher prices, our discussions with market participants indicate that conditions in the spot market have not improved at all since last month. Higher copper prices have also attracted more scrap into the market so this is also acting as a dampener on cathode demand. While the lack of spot business means there are few premium quotations, we assess the US premium for cathode delivered in the Midwest is in the range of 6.0¢/lb and 7.0¢/lb, down slightly from last month’s quotation. European conditions are little changed, so we continue to assess the premium in the range of $60/t and $80/t. In China, the premium for imported cathode is lower than last month, with quotations between $50/t and $60/t. As of 28th September, total exchange stocks amounted to 431,633 tonnes, which was slightly below the 434,860 tonnes recorded on 24th August. LME stocks declined during most of September, but in the last two weeks, they began to increase once again. Cancellations are still rather high and on 28th September these were recorded at 39,250 tonnes, representing 17.6% of total LME holdings. Inventories on both the SHFE and COMEX were on a rising trend over the last month. warehouse stocks. These estimated are supplied by CRU’s Beijing office and are reported regularly in the _Copper China Fortnightly_ supplement. Bonded warehouse stocks, excluding those which are reported as SHFE stocks, are currently estimated at 630,000 tonnes, which is a significant increase on the 521,000 tonnes reported last month. We understand that most of this volume is in the hands of Chinese traders and is being used as collateral in financing arrangements. The implication of this is that if stock levels in the rest of the world fall further, pushing the LME price high enough, these bonded warehouse stocks should become available to meet demand requirements anywhere in the world. As the chart illustrates, these bonded warehouse stocks represent more than 60% of the world’s visible cathode stocks. Thus, if there is a pick-up in demand elsewhere in the world that cannot be met by new production, both LME prices, and cathode premiums, are likely to rise in order to attract metal into the market where it is needed. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 4 of 19 October 2012 Copper Monitor www. crugroup.com #### Price gains capped by market fundamentals As we noted previously, the improvement in sentiment among investors has been largely responsible for the gains experienced by the copper price during September. Price direction in the near term will largely depend on the euro, the economic outlook, and the performance of mine supply. It will be difficult for copper prices to move significantly higher because the sources of upward price pressure are fading. Investor sentiment has already shifted. The euro has gained ground against the US dollar, but has not been able to push above $1.30/€ because market participants recognize that the sovereign debt and banking crises have not been definitively resolved. Last week, there were protests in Spain regarding more fiscal austerity next year. Greece has, once again, had difficulty passing a budget which would ensure that the country received another tranche of bailout funds. Both of these events stand as stark reminders that the battle over EU institutional stability is still being waged. The markets expect the EU to appoint a single bank regulator by the end of this year. Failure to deliver may cause investors to liquidate their new net long and the level of confidence they have in the euro will determine whether the price reverts to the tr

ading range experienced between May and September, or falls further towards $6,800/t, which we last saw in October 2011. 

Although the market’s perception about future economic growth has become more optimistic, participants will require ongoing confirmation that a recovery is truly underway. Data that are outside the realm of expectation, either positive or negative, will produce a reaction from investors, and cause continued volatility in the copper price. The most recent PMI data for China and the US point to stabilization in the manufacturing sectors of both economies. The economic data for Europe, however, are still very discouraging and we estimate that consumption will have declined by 3.3% y-o-y by the end of 2012, with Western Europe showing a 3.7% decline. In terms of the US, all eyes will be on the US Congress, which needs to get control of the nation’s budget deficit before a series of automatic spending cuts and tax increases go into effect on 1<sup>st</sup> January (the so-called “fiscal cliff”).  Negotiations are already underway in the Senate, but progress will be minimal until the outcomes of the 6<sup>th</sup> November presidential and congressional elections are known.  Failure to deliver a timely agreement will have severe consequences for the US economy.  As for China, the copper market is clearly oversupplied, particularly in the context of anticipated demand growth of about 6.0% next year, which represents a volume increase of about 490,000 tonnes. There is currently more than enough stock in China to cover next year’s demand increase. Thus, the extent to which China imports cathode to fulfil new demand and/or utilizes its available stocks, will have implications for the LME copper price. In the short-term, however, China is unlikely to provide significant upward pressure on the copper price. 

Last, but certainly not least, is the issue of mine supply.  Production in 2012 was stronger than expected, and there have been relatively few disruptions to mine supply this year.  As a result, CRU has continually reduced its disruption allowances and revised our supply forecasts higher. Long-term investors will be watching carefully for signs of either extended oversupply or shortage before committing their funds to the copper market once again.

### Consumption trends 

#### Recovery stalls in flat rolled market 

After registering a modest improvement in Q1 2012, the recovery in the flat rolled copper market faltered in Q2. World consumption of copper and copper alloy plate sheet, strip and foil (PSSF) declined by 6.7% y-o-y and 2.4% y-oy respectively.  Much of the weakness stemmed from the European market, where the ongoing sovereign debt crisis is severely restricting end-user demand.  But weak consumption is not confined to Europe alone.  Japanese demand for both copper and copper alloy flat rolled products fell

sharply in Q2 as did consumption in several other Asian countries, most notably Taiwan. Even in China demand is soft, with consumption of copper alloy PSSF registering a decline in Q2. In response to lacklustre demand in all the key consuming regions, producers of flat rolled products reduced output. One factor behind the lacklustre levels of Chinese **75 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2** demand is weaker consumption of foil for use in **09 10 11 12 Data: CRU** producing copper clad laminate (CCL). CCL is consumed in the manufacture of printed circuit boards (PCB), which are used in a variety of electronic products such as computers, home appliances, lighting and communication equipment. According to data released by **Antaike** , Chinese CCL production expanded rapidly during the last decade, rising at an average annual rate of 21% since 2000. More recently, however, Chinese demand for foil in this application has fallen, down by 6.3% in 2011 to a level of 178,000t and a further reduction is anticipated in 2012. The decline reflects the trend towards using thinner gauges of foil in electronic applications as well as the move towards using fewer individual components within each electronic device. As a result, spare capacity exists in the Chinese copper foil market, especially at the lower quality end of the spectrum. Japanese consumption of copper PSSF and copper alloy PSSF declined sharply in Q2, down by 23% and 21% respectively on a y-o-y basis. Producers of copper PSSF have been quick to respond, cutting output by 13% y-o-y in Q1 and by a further 22% y-o-y in Q2. Despite these cuts, inventories of copper PSSF have continued to rise in each month to June. By contrast, the copper alloy PSSF market is in better shape. Despite the slump in demand in Q2, offtake was strong in Q1 and inventories of copper alloy PSSF have followed a downward path in the months to July. **Furukawa Electric** announced that it planned to start production of electrolytic copper foil at its new plant in Taiwan in Q3. The facility, which will produce foil for use in automotive lithium ion batteries, will enable Furukawa to shift increas

ing quantities of foil production from Japan to Taiwan.  Japanese foil manufacturers have suffered from a strong yen and high electricity costs in recent years, leaving them uncompetitive compared with producers in South Korea and Taiwan.

### Industry News 

#### Consumption 



- The National Development and Reform Commission of China approved 25 new urban rail transit and intercity rail projects in investment programmes worth RMB800B (US$127B), it was announced on 5<sup>th</sup> September.  The projects are expected to be completed in the next three to eight years.  Local governments will be major investors, although banks loans are also expected to constitute a significant portion of the total investment funding.  This comes after reports emerged in July that approximately RMB300B of China’s RMB448B annual railway budget had yet to be spent. 



- **Amer International Group** , a Chinese copper products fabricator, announced on 14<sup>th</sup> September that it is building a 500,000t/y copper wire and rod plant in Guangdong Province. The facility will have additional capacity to produce 100,000t/y of copper alloy products. **Amer** expects to bring the operation on stream by 2015 and the combined investment cost amounts to RMB11.2B (US$1.8B).  It currently has an attributable wirerod production capacity of 250,000t/y through its subsidiary’s plant situated in the Tongling Economic and Technological Development Zone.  The company is targeting a wirerod production capacity of 1.5Mt/y via two further projects. 



- China’s **Far East Holding Group** , which runs one of the country’s largest cable manufacturing operations, acquired a 60% stake in **Shengda Copper** , a leading Chinese copper semis producer based in Taixing, Jiangsu province.  The companies signed the investment contract, worth $6.6M, on 15<sup>th</sup> September. 



- **Shanghai Shenghua Cable** , a large cablemaker based in China, said on 21<sup>st</sup> September that it would not be increasing its copper stocks prior to China’s single week holiday in October.  The company attributed this unusual buying behaviour to the recent copper price rise and to cashflow problems caused by a high level of credit being extended to its customers. **Shenghua** added that it has experienced normal sales this year but expects lower orders for the remainder of the year due to seasonally poor weather conditions in northern China.  It has been reducing finished stock levels for the weakest performing industries, which it says are coal mining and ship building, whereas, low voltage cable for buildings is being seen as a more resilient sector. 



- Shanghai Metals Market (SMM) reported on 24<sup>th</sup> September that the average operating rates of copper cablemakers in China rose by 10 percentage points to reach 78.7% in August.  Newly tendered contracts from the **State Grid Cor

poration of China** (SGCC) in July and August were the key underlying factor.  Figures from the National Bureau of Statistics also indicate that cable output rose by 2.5% m-o-m to 3.53M km in August.  An August survey of Chinese copper wirerod fabricators by SMM also showed a 2 percentage point increase in the industry’s average utilisation rate from the previous month, to 75%.

#### Mine Production 



- **Glencore** upped its offer for its proposed merger of equals with **Xstrata** on 7<sup>th</sup> September, from 2.80 to 3.05 new shares for each existing **Xstrata** share.  However, under the proposed terms, the current CEO of **Glencore** , Ivan Glasenberg, would (after 6 months) lead the merged company, rather than **Xstrata** CEO Mick Davis who had previously been nominated to take charge. **Glencore’s** move follows pressure from **Xstrata** shareholders, including **Qatar Holdings** , which opposed the initial terms of the merger. **Glencore** currently owns 34% of Xstrata and the revised deal is valued at US$80B.  On 1<sup>st</sup> October, **Xstrata’s** board recommended shareholders to accept **Glencore’s** improved merger terms. 



- On 11<sup>th</sup> September, Julius Malema, a politician expelled from the governing ANC party of South Africa in April 2012, called for a national strike at all mining operations.  The development followed a number of strikes over pay at platinum and gold mines taking place since August. The situation escalated on 17<sup>th</sup> August, when 34 miners were shot dead and a further 78 were injured when police opened fire on protesters at the Marikana platinum mine, which in the prior week took the lives of ten people.  Malema was charged with money laundering on 26<sup>th</sup> September but his supporters claim the corruption case is politically motivated. Meanwhile unrest continues across the country's minerals sector. 



- Indonesia is asking mining companies to pay higher royalties of 10% as part of negotiations to extend the companies’ mining contracts.  In January 2012 the government of Indonesia formed a team to review the mining contracts. It was announced on 19<sup>th</sup> September that, as part of the negotiations, the government would seek royalties for metals similar to those paid by coal companies, which currently stand at 13.5%. **PT Freeport Indonesia** currently pays 1% as royalty for mining gold and 3.5% for copper. 



- **Carmen Copper Corp** , Philippines’ largest copper exporter, said on 21<sup>st</sup> September that it expects to sell 40,000t of copper in 2012, and improve its copper delivery by 30% or more in 2013.  The company is on track to expand its mill operations from 42,000tpd to 60,000tpd in 2013.  Over 90% of copper shipments from the company currently go to China but it is currently in talks with the **PASAR** smelter in Philippines to sell it concentra

tes in the future. 



- The end of a 30 day strike at Antofagasta port was announced on 21<sup>st</sup> September.  The temporary disruption forced producers shipping out of the port, including **Antofagasta Minerals** , **Barrick** and **BHP Billiton** to take their cargoes to Tocopilla port, causing delays in copper shipments. Premiums in Europe, where consumers are keeping inventories very low, were affected by the delays, reaching $96.25 per tonne on 27<sup>th</sup> September.

#### Exploration and Development 



- On 4<sup>th</sup> September, **Codelco** announced that construction had commenced on the access tunnels to a new mining level at the **El Teniente** underground copper mine in Chile.  This marks the start of a US$3.5B expansion project at the mine that aims to extend the mine life by 50 years. The new mining level is located 300m deeper than the current mining operations and the company expects to begin extracting ore in 2017. **El Teniente** is expected to produce approximately 400,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2012 and the expansion project will enable the company to maintain this production level beyond 2017. 



- On 14<sup>th</sup> September reports emerged that **PanAust** and **Codelco** had postponed their **Inca de Oro** copper and gold project due to higher energy costs.  Construction at the $600M **Inca de Oro** project was scheduled to begin in 2013 and the mine would have produced 40,000 ounces of gold and 50,000 metric tons of copper a year at full capacity.  Chile has the highest generation costs in the region, while a series of delays and cancellation of power projects could induce further increases in energy costs. 



- On 18<sup>th</sup> September, it was announced that first commercial production has commenced at the **Duobaoshan** copper-molybdenum project in Heilongjiang province, China.  The operation is currently in Phase I, which is set to achieve copper-in-concentrate production of 30,000t/y upon completion of ramp-up.  The start-up of the Phase II expansion is targeted for H1 2014, adding a further 20,000t/y of production upon reaching full capacity.  The final expansion stage, Phase III, is expected to take start-up in 2017, adding 15,000t/y to overall production capacity.  The mine is a joint venture between **Zijin Mining Group Northeast Asia** (51%) and **Heilongjiang Heilong Mining Joint Stock** (49%). 



- On 20<sup>th</sup> September Zambia's environmental management agency allowed **NFC Africa Mining Corp** , a subsidiary of **China Non-ferrous Metal Mining & Construction Group** , to proceed with its **South East Ore Body** project.  The $832M copper project will add 60,000 tonnes to the country's annual output of the metal.  The project is located 400km northwest of Lusaka and has reserves of more than 76 M tonnes of copper at an average grade of 2.18%.  Building will start

this year. 



- **Southern Copper** announced on 1<sup>st</sup> October that it will decide in January if it will go forward with its US$1.2B **Los Chancas** project in Peru. **Los Chancas** has resources of 355M tonnes, with copper content of 0.62%, molybdenum of 0.05% and gold 0.039 g/t. 



- **Xstrata Copper** announced on 18<sup>th</sup> September that it would rely on an independent valuer to determine the amount it should pay for a stake in **Altona Mining’s Roseby** project, after the companies failed to agree on a price. **Xstrata** has an option to acquire a 51% stake in the project, located near Mt. Isa, in Australia. **Roseby** is one of Australia's largest undeveloped copper resources and according to the feasibility study it will produce 39,000t/y of copper and

#### Smelting and Refining 



- On 20<sup>th</sup> September, a senior official at **PASAR** , a majority owned subsidiary of **Glencore** , confirmed rumours of a US$600M expansion of its **Leyte** smelter in the Philippines.  The expansion is set to double the plant’s production capacity from the current level of 215,000t/y refined copper.  Final approval of the project is expected to take place in early 2013, if not before the end of this year.  Construction work may go ahead as early as May 2013, with an estimated development period of 2-3 years. **Glencore** has also revealed plans to build a 200MW coal-fired power plant near the operation in order to lower energy costs.  In 2011, Leyte produced 164,000t of copper cathode, however, a six-month outage caused by a January fire at the plant may see 2012 production fall to as little at 80,000t. 



- **Codelco’s Chuquicamata** smelter in Chile restarted operations on 15<sup>th</sup> September following a 53-day maintenance shutdown.  The extended downtime was purportedly necessitated by problems with the lining of the plant’s flash furnace.  The plant is equipped to produce up to 500,000t/y of copper blister from concentrate sourced from the nearby **Chuquicamata** mine. Last year, the smelter produced an estimated 290,000t of copper blister. 



- China’s Yunnan province government will purportedly stockpile 300,000 tonnes of industrial metals from local producers, including 20,000t of copper, with the aim of absorbing some of the surplus in the market and improving domestic spot prices.  Smelters will put physical metal into warehouses monitored by the provincial government and will receive loans from local banks equivalent to the market value of the stocks, with the interest paid by the provincial government.
